_comment: FICTIONAL worked-example policy for the fictional client 'Copperline Support Co.' — generated and evaluated by generate-example-trail.mjs against the real GhostGuard engine in ~/workspace/ghostguard/dist. Not a real client's policy.

rules.note: Locked: the agent never spends money, whoever asks.
Locked: the agent never deletes records.
Anything leaving the business routes to the owner, not the run's approver.
Internal comms still ask a human first.
Deploying a helpdesk macro/configuration change asks first.
Publishing a KB article asks first.
Unattended runs are held stricter: consequential classes ask even where a person at the keyboard would be allowed.
Standing approval: drafting a ticket reply (no send) is pre-approved within this rule's bounds.
Reads execute freely and are recorded.
Local writes by a person-initiated run are allowed.
Network writes by a person-initiated run are allowed; routine runs ask (routine-consequential-asks).
Tool execution by a person-initiated run is allowed; routine runs ask.
